info.title: SendKuy API
info.summary: Send WhatsApp, SMS and email from your own code.
info.description:
One key, one set of endpoints, three channels. Every object carries a
prefixed id you can store and send back, every list is cursor-paginated,
and every write is idempotent.

Ids are opaque. `msg_` is a message, `con_` a contact, `cmp_` a campaign —
the prefix is part of the contract, so read them as strings and never
parse what comes after the underscore.

origin.description: The SendKuy API host. Change it only to reach a proxy or a mock server in tests.

get.summary: Read the account behind this key
Read this period's usage per channel

200.description: Usage for the running subscription cycle.

get.description:
Newest first, cursor-paginated. Filters narrow the list; they do not
change the shape of what comes back.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only messages in this state. `delivered` includes WhatsApp messages
that were already read; `read` narrows to those.

post.summary: Send one message to one or more recipients
post.description:
One call, one body, one channel, many recipients — and one `message`
object back per recipient. A message is one row of delivery: one
person, one status. Sending to three numbers returns three objects.

Every recipient, its sender, and the credit for all of them are checked
before anything is sent. A missing contact or group, a contact without
an address on the channel, no sender for one of the recipients, or too
little credit refuses the whole call and nobody receives anything.

One recipient is sent while you wait, and its `status` is the outcome.
More than one recipient (a `grp_` group counts as its members) is
accepted, answered at once as `queued`, and sent in the background,
paced per number to keep it healthy. Follow each message with webhooks
or `GET /messages/{id}`. For bulk sends use several `to` or
`POST /messages/batch`: both are paced for you. Looping over single
sends is not.

Recipients must be in E.164 form, with the `+`. A local number is
refused rather than guessed: guessing the wrong country sends a
stranger a message and bills you for it.
post.x-contract-reason: Sends real messages and spends real credit.

value.body: Your order is on its way.

201.description:
One object per recipient, in the order you gave them. No `meta`:
this is a list, not a page — nothing was cut off.

post.summary: Send up to 500 independent messages in one call
post.description:
Not a repeat of `POST /messages`. Each element carries its own channel,
recipient and body, and each one is answered on its own row: `index`,
the `id` that was created, and `error` when that element failed. One
mistyped number does not throw away the 499 that were fine.

The rows carry ids, not message objects. Every message is accepted as
`queued` and sent in the background, paced per number; read it back
with `GET /messages/{id}` or follow it with webhooks. Status is 200, not
201, because a batch that failed entirely still answers row by row.

Too little credit and a channel your plan does not include are reported
on the element's row (`insufficient_credits`, `channel_not_in_plan`),
not as an error for the whole call.
post.x-contract-reason: Sends real messages and spends real credit.

messages.body: Your order is on its way.

200.description: One row per element, in the order you sent them.

post.summary: Cancel a message that has not gone out yet
post.description:
Only a message still `queued` or `scheduled` can be cancelled. One that
has already left is refused with `request_refused` — there is nothing
to call back.

Creates a fresh delivery for the same recipient and body. The original
row keeps its own status; this answers with the new one.

On a WhatsApp device we ask WhatsApp again before charging. A number
that has no WhatsApp account is refused with `validation_failed` and
costs nothing.
post.x-contract-reason: Sends a real message and spends real credit.

post.summary: Check which numbers are on WhatsApp
post.description:
Asks WhatsApp, through one of your WhatsApp devices, whether each number
has an account. Free: it spends no credit and does not count against
your daily limit, but it has its own ceiling of 10 calls a minute per
key.

Answers are shared and kept for 30 days, so a number checked recently
comes back without asking WhatsApp again.

Only a WhatsApp device can check. A Cloud API number cannot.
post.x-contract-reason: Asks WhatsApp about real numbers through a connected device.

200.description: One row per number, in the order you sent them.

post.description:
Creates a code, sends it through the first channel in `channels` that
has a sender, and answers at once. When a WhatsApp device sends it but
no delivery receipt arrives within 30 seconds, or a send fails later,
the same code goes out on the next channel.

Each message spends the credit of its own channel. A channel that is
skipped spends nothing.
post.x-contract-reason: Sends a real message to a real number.

201.description:
The verification, with the outcome of the first send. When no
channel could send the code, `status` is already `failed`.

post.description:
A matching code approves the verification and is used up. A wrong code
answers `422 verification_code_invalid`; the error carries no
`checks_remaining`, so read it with `GET /verifications/{id}`. Five
wrong codes fail it. A code past its `ttl` is refused with
`verification_expired`, and that check is what closes the verification
and cancels its unsent messages.

get.summary: Read the status of background work
get.description:
Guarded by a key, but by **no scope at all** — the only route in v1
that is. A job is born from a call whose scope was already checked, so
asking for its progress needs nothing further. Do not infer scopes
from the pattern of other routes here.

post.description:
At least one of `whatsapp`, `sms` or `email` is required.

A number, email or `external_id` that already belongs to one of your
contacts updates that contact instead of creating a second one, and
the answer is `200` rather than `201`. `on_existing` decides what that
update may change. Saved numbers and emails are only ever replaced
through a matching `external_id` with `update`. When the values in the
request belong to different contacts, nothing is written and the
answer is `validation_failed`, naming those contacts.

200.description: The contact you already had, matched by number, email or external_id.

post.summary: Import up to 1000 contacts in the background
post.description:
Answers `202` with a `job`, not with contacts: nothing has been created
yet when the call returns. Poll `GET /jobs/{id}` to watch it finish and
to read the per-row errors.

Each row is matched the way `POST /contacts` matches, with one
`on_existing` for the whole call, so sending the same rows twice
creates nothing the second time. The finished job reports `counts`.

202.description: The job that will do the work.

get.summary: Find a contact by phone number or by your own id
get.description:
A separate path from `GET /contacts/{id}`, not an id that happens to
read as a word. Pass `phone` or `external_id`; when both are sent,
`external_id` decides. A number must be in E.164 form; a local number
is refused rather than guessed. A number matches the WhatsApp column
first, then the SMS column.

parameters.name: external_id
parameters.description: The id you gave the contact in your own system. Matched exactly, case included.

200.description: The contact using that number or carrying that id.

patch.description: Only the fields you send are changed.

200.description: The contact, as it is now.

delete.description:
Removes the contact and its group memberships. Scheduled messages to it
are cancelled first and their credit is returned. Messages already queued
still go out, and messages already sent stay in your history with the
address they went to.

get.summary: List the attributes defined on your contacts
get.description:
Every definition at once — there is no cursor and no `meta`, because
nothing is cut off. Use it to read the flat `attributes` map that each
contact carries.

named.summary: A name is all it takes

200.description: The group, as it is now.

delete.description: The contacts in it are not deleted; they end up with no group.

200.description: Confirmation that the group is gone.

post.description:
A contact can belong to any number of groups, so adding it here leaves
its other groups alone. `added` counts the contacts that were not in the
group yet.

delete.summary: Take contacts out of a group
delete.description:
This `DELETE` carries a request body, which is unusual enough to look
like a mistake. It is not: what is being removed is the membership of
a list of contacts, and that list does not fit in the path. The
contacts themselves are untouched.

value.name: Order shipped
value.body: Your order is on its way.

patch.description:
`channel` cannot be changed and is refused by name. A template's body
lives under a different key per channel, so switching it would silently
change the meaning of everything that uses the template.

200.description: The template, as it is now.
Confirmation that the template is gone.

get.summary: List the gateways your messages can leave through
get.description:
Your own gateways, then the SIM cards in the Android phones you paired.
SendKuy's shared senders are not listed, even when your plan lends
them — leave `gateway_id` out when sending and we pick one.

A SIM keeps its id while it stays in the same phone. Pairing your
account with a different phone lists its SIMs under new ids.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Only gateways on this channel. `sms` includes your Android SIMs.

200.description: A page of endpoints, each with `secret_preview` rather than its secret.

post.description:
The only response that carries the signing secret in full. Store it
when you receive it — every later read answers with `secret_preview`,
and there is no way to ask for it again.

201.description: The endpoint, with its secret. The only time you see it.

200.description: The endpoint, with `secret_preview` rather than its secret.
The endpoint, as it is now.
Confirmation that the endpoint is gone.

get.summary: Read the delivery history of an endpoint
get.description:
One row per attempt, newest first. The payload we sent is not
included — it can carry message text, and this list is here to answer
"why did it fail".

Without `stats`. Counting dispatch rows for every campaign on a page is
work nobody asked for — read one campaign to get its numbers.

post.description: Created as a `draft`. Nothing goes out until you start it.

get.summary: Read one campaign, with its numbers
get.description:
The only campaign response that carries `stats`. The list endpoint
leaves it out.

patch.description:
Legal while the campaign is `draft`, `scheduled` or `paused`. A running
or finished campaign is refused with `request_refused` — its dispatch
rows already exist, and changing the message underneath them would
send something nobody approved.

200.description: The campaign, as it is now.
Confirmation that the campaign is gone.

get.summary: List what a campaign is sending, per contact
get.description:
A dispatch is the plan to send to one contact, not a message.
`message_id` is null until the row has been processed. A recurring
campaign has one set of dispatches per run; this lists the latest run
unless `run` says otherwise.

parameters.name: run
parameters.description: Run number to list. Defaults to the latest run.

get.summary: Read the messages in a conversation
get.description:
These are `conversation_message` objects with `cms_` ids, not the
`msg_` delivery rows you get from `GET /messages`. Different things,
different prefixes.

200.description: A page of messages in the thread.

post.description: Sets `unread_count` to zero. Answers with the conversation.

Answers `201` with the **`conversation_message`** that was created —
not the conversation, and not a `msg_` delivery row.
post.x-contract-reason: Sends a real message to the contact.

201.description: The message that was added to the thread.

get.summary: List the runs of one workflow

post.description:
Answers with a report — how many workflows were triggered and how many
contacts were enrolled — not with the workflow. One call can start
more than one workflow, because the trigger matches on conditions.
post.x-contract-reason: Runs a customer's workflow, which sends and enrolls for real.

get.description:
Stands on its own, outside `/workflows/{id}/executions`, and is guarded
by the same `automation:read` scope.

post.description: Legal from `draft` and `scheduled`. An instant campaign builds one dispatch row per eligible contact and moves to `running`; it is refused with `402 insufficient_credits` when the balance does not cover them, and with `403 request_refused` when the plan no longer includes one of its channels. A scheduled or recurring campaign moves to `scheduled`, and its recipients are counted from the group when each run starts. Nothing is sent by this call itself.

200.description: The campaign, in its new state.

post.description: Legal from `running`. Dispatches already handed to a worker still go out; nothing new is picked up.

200.description: The campaign, in its new state.

post.description: Legal from `paused`. Calling it on a campaign that never started is refused — there is nothing to resume. The campaign stays `paused` when the balance still does not cover the rest of the run (`402 insufficient_credits`) or the plan no longer includes one of its channels (`403 request_refused`).

200.description: The campaign, in its new state.

post.description: Legal from `draft`, `scheduled`, `running` and `paused`. A completed campaign cannot be cancelled after the fact.

200.description: The campaign, in its new state.

bearerAuth.description:
`Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...`. Keys in the query string or the
request body are refused — a URL is logged by every proxy it passes,
and that is how customer keys leak.

A key carries scopes. A call outside them answers 403 with
`insufficient_scope` and names the scope it wanted.

x-scopes.account:read: Read your plan, credits and rate limit.
x-scopes.campaigns:write: Create, change, start, pause, resume, cancel and delete campaigns.
x-scopes.contacts:read: Read contacts and the attributes defined on them.
x-scopes.contacts:write: Create, change, bulk-import and delete contacts.
x-scopes.gateways:read: Read the gateways your messages can leave through.
x-scopes.groups:write: Create and change groups, and move contacts in and out.
x-scopes.inbox:write: Mark a conversation read, and reply to it.
x-scopes.numbers:read: Check which phone numbers have a WhatsApp account.
x-scopes.verifications:write: Send one-time codes and check them.
x-scopes.webhooks:read: Read webhook endpoints and their delivery history.
x-scopes.webhooks:write: Create, change and delete webhook endpoints.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20, capped at 100.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Any unique string, one per logical request. Retrying with the same key
returns the first answer instead of doing the work twice, and answers
with `Idempotent-Replay: true`. Every answer is remembered, refusals
included, except `rate_limit_exceeded` (`429`) and a server error
(`5xx`) that left nothing behind. A server error after a message was
handed over is remembered as that message, so the retry returns it
instead of sending again. A key belongs to your account, across
endpoints and API keys.

PathId.name: id
PathId.description: The prefixed id of the object.

type.description:
Your keys are `user` keys. `admin` keys belong to SendKuy staff, not
to an account. For them
`plan`, `credits` and `usage` come back null rather than missing —
a shape that disappears forces the caller to guess.

rate_limit.description: Requests per minute this key may make.

scopes.description: The scopes of the key that made this call, sorted. Other keys on the same account are not listed.

ErrorCode.description: Every error this API can answer with.

oneOf.description: No Authorization header, or one that is not `Bearer`.
The token does not match any key we issued.
The key existed and was revoked from the dashboard.
The key carried an expiry and it has passed.
The account behind the key has no running plan.
The account behind the key is suspended, in the trash, or being deleted.
The key is valid but was not issued the scope this route needs.
The plan does not include the channel you asked to send on.

Not enough credit for this send. 402 rather than 403 because this is
the one refusal you fix by paying, not by changing the request.
A field is missing, malformed, or not allowed here. `param` names it.

Nothing on this channel can send for you right now: no gateway of your
own is connected, or the shared senders your plan lends are all offline.
The message says which.

A sender was found for this call and it did not answer: a WhatsApp
device that is disconnected or reconnecting. Retry shortly.
The code does not match. The message says how many attempts are left.
The verification passed its ttl. Start a new one.
The verification is already approved, failed or cancelled.
Well-formed, but refused for a reason the message states.
No object of that type carries that id in your account.
The path exists, the method does not.
That key was used for a request with a different body.
The first request with that key has not finished. Retry shortly.
Too many requests this minute. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.
Our fault. The `X-Request-Id` header identifies the call.

message.description: One sentence, in English, naming the problem and the fix.

param.description: Present when one field caused it. Names that field.

period.description:
The running subscription cycle, not the calendar month. Docs say so
because a number you cannot line up with an invoice is not a number.

has_more.description: Whether another page exists after this one.

next_cursor.description:
Pass it back as `starting_after` for the next page. Treat it as
opaque: do not parse, compare or construct it.

Message.description:
One message is one line of delivery: one recipient, one status. Sending
to three numbers gives you three of these, not one with three addresses.

status.description:
`delivered` means the provider accepted the message, not that the
phone received it. When the phone reports back we fill
`delivered_at`, and `read_at` once it is read. `read` is WhatsApp
only: the recipient opened it.

`queued` is where a message to several recipients, a batch element,
or an automation step waits for its turn on the number that sends it.

`queued` also covers a message moving to another of your senders after
its own failed. `scheduled` also covers a message sent to a group, or
scheduled with `schedule_at`, while every sender on its channel is
failing: we try again every hour for up to 24 hours, then it fails.

`sent`, `opened`, `clicked`, `replied` and `bounced` only ever appear
on messages born from a campaign — the tables behind single sends do
not record them. That is a limit of the system, not a gap in the
mapping, so do not wait for them on a message you sent yourself.

to.description: The recipient, as stored on the contact for this channel.

subject.description: Email only. Null on every other channel.

campaign_id.description: Set when this message came from a campaign.

delivered_at.description:
WhatsApp only: when the recipient's phone received the message. Null
until the receipt arrives, and always null for SMS and email.

read_at.description: WhatsApp only. When the recipient read the message.

error.description:
What the gateway answered, and only when the row failed. On a
successful send it is null even though the gateway did reply.

SendMessageRequest.description:
One body, one channel, many recipients. Fields that do not belong to the
channel you picked are refused by name rather than ignored: a caller on
the wrong channel should find out on the first try, not after the message
went out without its subject.

to.description:
Up to 100 recipients. On `sms` and `whatsapp` every entry must be
E.164 with the leading `+`. A local number is refused rather than
guessed: guessing the wrong country sends a stranger a message and
bills you for it.

media.description: WhatsApp only. One attachment, fetched from a URL you host.

attachments.description:
Email only, at most ten. Each one is a download we make while your
call is open, which is why the number is capped.

gateway_id.description:
Optional. Left out, we pick among the live senders on this channel —
your own gateways, or SendKuy's shared ones when your plan lends them —
and keep each recipient on the number that reached them before. On
WhatsApp that means a number connected by QR or the Chrome extension;
the Cloud API is only picked for a template message. An account with
only a Cloud API number gets `no_sender_available` for a plain
WhatsApp message.

Left out, a message whose sender fails because of the gateway itself
(a disconnected device, a phone without signal, credentials or balance
the provider refuses, a provider outage) moves to your next live sender
on the same channel, up to five senders. It keeps its id and is not
charged again. Your own senders come first; SendKuy's shared ones follow
only once all of yours were tried and your plan lends them. A failure
that may already have reached the recipient, or that every sender would
hit (a number not on WhatsApp, an invalid address), is not retried
elsewhere. When no sender is left, a message to one address fails and its
credit comes back; a message to a group waits for a sender (see
`status`).

Naming one sends through exactly that gateway, and it is never swapped. A `sim_` id names one
SIM in your Android phone and works only with `channel: sms`; on any
other channel it is refused with `validation_failed`. On WhatsApp a
template that belongs to a number fixes the sender; naming a different
gateway is refused with `validation_failed`. When your plan sends this
channel only through SendKuy's shared senders, naming a gateway is
refused with `validation_failed` too.

schedule_at.description:
Send later instead of now. The message comes back `scheduled`.
Include a time zone offset, for example `2026-11-01T09:00:00+07:00`
or `2026-11-01T02:00:00Z`; a time without one is refused with
`validation_failed`.

ListEnvelope.description:
A list that is not a page. There is no cursor and no `meta` because
nothing was cut off: three of the four endpoints that answer this way
return one row per element you sent, and the fourth returns every
attribute you have defined.

SendMessageBatchRequest.description:
Up to 500 independent messages in one call. The shape of every field
in every element is validated up front, and a mistake there refuses the
whole call with `validation_failed`. The recipient, the gateway, the
channel in your plan and the credit are checked per element, so one bad
number does not throw away the 499 that were fine.

to.description: One recipient per element, not a list.

schedule_at.description: Same rules as `schedule_at` on `POST /messages`, including the time zone offset.

BatchRowError.description:
Why this one element failed. It is deliberately not the `error` object
the rest of the API returns: there is no `doc_url`, and `param` is
present but may be null. One element failing does not fail the call, so
this never appears at the top level.

BatchRow.description:
One row per element you sent, in the order you sent them. Exactly one of
`id` and `error` is set.

index.description: Position in the `messages` array you sent.

id.description: The message that was created, or null if this element failed.

numbers.description:
Up to 50 numbers, E.164 with the leading `+`. Spaces and dashes after
the `+` are fine. A local number without the country code is answered
with `registered: null` rather than guessed.

gateway_id.description:
Optional. The WhatsApp device that asks. Left out, we pick one of your
live devices, or a SendKuy device when your plan lends them. A Cloud
API number or an Android SIM cannot check and is refused with
`validation_failed`.

number.description: The number exactly as you sent it, so you can match rows.

registered.description:
Whether the number has a WhatsApp account. `null` when the entry is
not a valid number in E.164 form.

checked_at.description:
When WhatsApp was last asked about this number. Answers are shared and
kept for 30 days, so this can be older than your call.

to.description: E.164. Required when `channels` includes whatsapp or sms.

brand.description: Shown in the message. No braces, pipes or angle brackets. Defaults to your account name.

message_id.description: The message that carried the code, readable with `GET /messages/{id}`.

outcome.description:
`skipped` means no sender or credit was available on this channel.
A channel your plan lacks never gets an attempt: the request is
refused with `channel_not_in_plan`. `undelivered` means a WhatsApp
device sent it but no delivery receipt came within 30 seconds.

Verification.description:
One code sent to one person, through the first channel in `channels`
that delivers. The code itself is never returned.

channel.description: The channel of the latest attempt.

Job.description:
Work that runs after the call returns. Poll `GET /jobs/{id}` until
`status` is `succeeded` or `failed`.

errors.description:
Always a list, never null: a caller checking for failures should not
have to tell "none yet" apart from "none at all".

counts.description:
What a finished `contacts.bulk` job did with its rows. `null` while
the job is still running, and for other job types. A conflict in
`errors` also names the contacts it collides with under `contacts`.

skipped.description: Rows that matched a contact and changed nothing.

conflicts.description: Rows whose number, email or external_id belong to different contacts.

group_ids.description:
Every group the contact belongs to. A contact can sit in any number
of groups, or in none.

external_id.description:
Your own id for this person, such as a CRM record. Unique within your
account. Case is kept and matched exactly.

attributes.description:
A flat map of the attributes you have defined, key to value. The type
of each one is answered once by `GET /contact-attributes` rather than
repeated on every contact — sending it back thousands of times would
be the same answer thousands of times.

SaveContactRequest.description:
On `POST` at least one address is required — a contact with no address
cannot be sent anything. On `PATCH` every field is optional and only the
ones you send are changed.

On `PATCH`, a number, email or `external_id` that another of your
contacts already uses is refused with `validation_failed`, naming that
contact. On `POST` it is matched instead; see `on_existing`.

on_existing.description:
Read on `POST` only: what happens when the number, email or
`external_id` already belongs to one of your contacts. `update`
replaces names and attributes, `fill_empty` only fills what is
empty, `skip` leaves them as they are. With every choice the
contact still joins the groups in `group_ids`.

group_ids.description:
The groups the contact should belong to. On `PATCH` it replaces the
contact's memberships with exactly this list, and an empty list takes
the contact out of every group. On `POST` it only adds: a contact that
already exists joins these groups and keeps the ones it was in. Leave
it out to keep the memberships as they are.

external_id.description:
Your own id for this person, such as a CRM record. Unique within your
account; surrounding spaces are trimmed and case is kept. Find the
contact by it later with `GET /contacts/lookup?external_id=`.

on_existing.description: Applies to every row, the same way as on `POST /contacts`.

ContactDeleted.description:
The contact is gone. Scheduled messages to it were cancelled first and
their credit returned; messages already sent keep their address in your
history.

ContactAttribute.description:
A definition, not a row — which is why it carries no prefixed id. It
tells you how to read the values you find under `attributes` on a contact.

key.description: The key as it appears in a contact's `attributes` map.

name.description: The same key, formatted for display.

contact_count.description: How many contacts are in the group right now.

Deleted.description:
What a `DELETE` answers. An empty body would force you to guess whether
the call worked, so the object that is gone says so itself.

GroupMembershipAdded.description:
Adding contacts to a group answers with the membership change, not with
the group. A contact keeps every other group it belongs to.

id.description: The group the contacts were added to.

added.description:
How many of the contacts were not in the group yet. Contacts that
already were are left as they are.

GroupMembershipRemoved.description:
Removing contacts from a group does not delete them, and they keep every
other group they belong to.

channel.description:
Fixed at creation. Changing it would move the body to a different
key and change the meaning of every place that uses the template,
so `PATCH` refuses it by name — make a new template instead.

subject.description: Email only. Null on every other channel.

body.description:
Stored under a different key per channel; it always comes back here
as `body`.

read_only.description:
True for a WhatsApp template on a SendKuy number your plan lends you.
Sending with it fixes the sender to that number; you cannot edit or
delete it.

SaveTemplateRequest.description:
`channel` is required on `POST` and prohibited on `PATCH`. `subject` is
accepted on `email` only, and refused by name elsewhere rather than
stored where nothing will ever read it.

Gateway.description:
A connection your messages leave through. Read-only over the API: there
is no `gateways:write` scope at all, because creating one needs
credentials and a verification flow that do not fit in a single call.
Set them up in the dashboard.

An Android SIM is listed as a gateway too, with a `sim_` id.

type.description:
Which provider or mechanism this gateway uses. `android` is a SIM
card in one of your paired Android phones.

address.description:
The sender number or address your recipients see — never the
credentials used to reach it. For a WhatsApp device it is the number
that linked, and null until a phone has linked. For an Android SIM it
is null: the phone does not report a number we can trust.

status.description:
For an Android SIM, `active` means the SIM may send and its phone is
connected right now.

is_default.description:
The gateway you marked as preferred in the dashboard. Sending without
a `gateway_id` spreads across every live gateway instead of always
using this one.

url.description:
`https://` only. The payload can carry the text of your customers'
messages, and plain http would send that in the clear.

events.description: Which events we call this endpoint for.

secret_preview.description:
The first characters of the signing secret, enough to tell two
endpoints apart and not enough to sign anything.

disabled_at.description: Set when repeated failures took the endpoint out of service.

secret.description:
The signing secret, in full. Present on `POST /webhooks` and nowhere
else — store it when you create the endpoint, because every later
read answers with `secret_preview` instead.

WebhookWithSecret.description:
A created webhook, which is the one time the secret comes back whole.
Deliberately a different schema from `Webhook`, for the same object.

`secret` is declared on `Webhook` itself and merely made required here,
rather than added in the `allOf` branch: `additionalProperties: false`
only ever sees the `properties` of the schema it sits in, so a field
introduced by a sibling branch would be rejected by the base.

WebhookDelivery.description:
One attempt at calling your endpoint. The payload we sent is not
included: it can contain message text, and this list exists to answer
"why did it fail", not to be a second copy of the content.

attempt.description: 1 for the first try, up to 6.

response_excerpt.description: The first 2048 bytes of what your endpoint answered.

until.description: Last day a run may start on, inclusive.

CampaignStats.description:
Counts roll up: a higher state implies every lower one was passed, so
`opened` includes what was clicked and replied. `delivered` counts a
successful send on email, which has no delivery receipt to wait for. On
WhatsApp a message moves to `delivered` when the phone receives it and
to `opened` when it is read.

by_channel.description: The same counts per channel, keyed by channel name.

group_id.description: The contact group this campaign sends to.

recurrence.description: How a recurring campaign repeats. `null` for instant and scheduled campaigns.

next_run_at.description: When the next run of a recurring campaign starts. `null` once it has no run left.

current_run.description: Number of the latest run, starting at 1. `null` for a draft.

paused_reason.description: Why the latest run is paused. `credits` and `plan` resume once you top up or change plan. `failed` means preparing the recipients failed; resuming tries again.

SaveCampaignRequest.description:
`name`, `channels` and `group_id` are required on `POST` and optional on
`PATCH`.

recurrence.description: Required when `type` is `recurring`, refused otherwise. Each run goes to everyone in the group at that moment.

CampaignWithStats.description:
What `GET /campaigns/{id}` answers. The list endpoint leaves `stats` out
— counting dispatch rows for every campaign on a page is work nobody
asked for — so do not expect it there.

CampaignDispatch.description:
A campaign dispatch is **not** a message. It is the plan to send to one
contact; `message_id` stays null until that plan has actually been
processed. This is the distinction most easily missed in the whole API.

message_id.description:
Null until the dispatch has been processed. A non-null value is a
`msg_` id you can read with `GET /messages/{id}`.

run.description: Number of the run this dispatch belongs to, starting at 1.

channel.description: The channel the conversation happens on.

status.description:
`active` for a conversation still in your inbox. Stored as a plain
string rather than a fixed set, so treat unknown values as opaque.

address.description:
The other side of the conversation: a phone number in E.164 form
for WhatsApp and SMS, or a lower-case email address. One address
on one of your devices is one conversation, so the same person
writing to two of your WhatsApp numbers is two conversations.
`null` only on conversations older than this field whose contact
was already gone.

contact_id.description:
The contact that owns `address` right now, looked up each time the
conversation is read. `null` when no contact has that address.
Changing a contact's number never moves an existing conversation;
it only changes which conversation this field points from.

ConversationMessage.description:
One message inside a conversation, and **not** the same thing as a
`message`. `msg_` ids point at delivery rows — one recipient, one status.
This is a line in a thread, so it carries its own prefix, `cms_`.

Workflow.description:
Read-only over the API, plus one action: you can trigger a workflow, but
you build it in the dashboard.

status.description: `active`, `paused` or `draft`. A plain string, not a closed set.

WorkflowExecution.description: One contact's run through one workflow.

WorkflowTrigger.description:
A report on what the trigger did, not the workflow itself. One call can
start more than one workflow, because the trigger matches on conditions
rather than on the id alone.

ReceivedMessage.description:
The `data` of a `message.received` event. It carries every field of a
`conversation_message` plus who wrote, on which channel and number, and
any media.

With incoming messages kept in the SendKuy inbox, `id` and
`conversation_id` point at the stored message and its thread. With
incoming messages forwarded to your webhook only, nothing is stored, so
both are `null`: reply with `POST /messages` to `from`. A forwarded
message that your endpoint never accepts after every retry is kept in the
inbox instead.

from.description: The sender, in E.164 for SMS and WhatsApp.

gateway_id.description: The number or gateway that received the message.

provider_message_id.description: The id the provider gave the message. Use it to skip a message you already handled.

url.description:
A link to the file. For a forwarded message it expires after
seven days, so copy the file. `null` when the channel does not
hand us the file.

Unauthorized.description:
`missing_api_key`, `invalid_api_key`, `api_key_revoked`, or
`api_key_expired`. The key itself is the problem, not the request.

Forbidden.description:
`insufficient_scope`, `subscription_expired`, `account_suspended`, or
`channel_not_in_plan`. The key is valid; it is not allowed to do this.
The message names the scope or the channel that was missing.

ValidationFailed.description:
`validation_failed`. A field is missing, malformed, or not allowed on
this endpoint. `param` names the field. On send endpoints the same
status also answers `no_sender_available` when nothing on the channel
can send for you, and `verification_code_invalid` when a code does not
match; the message says how many attempts are left.

RateLimited.description:
`rate_limit_exceeded`. Too many requests this minute for this key.
`Retry-After` says how long to wait; your limit comes from your plan.

InsufficientCredits.description:
`insufficient_credits`. The one refusal you fix by paying rather than
by changing the request, which is why it is 402 and not 403.

Conflict.description:
`idempotency_key_reused` when the key was used for a request with a
different body, or `idempotency_request_in_progress` when the first
request carrying it has not finished yet. Retry shortly for the second.
`verification_not_pending` when the verification is already approved,
failed or cancelled.

NotFound.description:
`resource_not_found`. No object of that type carries that id in your
account. Ids are scoped to the account behind the key, so an id that
works elsewhere answers 404 here rather than leaking that it exists.

RequestRefused.description:
`request_refused`. The request was well formed and still refused, for a
reason the message states — most often because the object is not in a
state where this action makes sense.

SenderUnavailable.description:
`sender_unavailable`. A sender was found for this call and it did not
answer: a WhatsApp device that is disconnected or reconnecting. Nothing
was spent. Retry shortly.

Gone.description: `verification_expired`: the verification passed its `ttl`. Start a new one.

X-Request-Id.description:
The id of this call, also written to `api_request_logs.request_id`.
Quote it when you report a problem and the row is found immediately.
Set by `ApiRequestContext`, on every response including errors.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Requests your key may make this minute. Comes from your plan.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current minute.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix seconds at which the window resets. Present on 429.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on 429.

Idempotent-Replay.description:
`true` when this response is the stored answer to an earlier request
carrying the same `Idempotency-Key`. Absent otherwise — the work was
done for this call. Set by `EnsureIdempotency`.

Deprecation.description:
Reserved. No v1 response carries it yet; it is listed because the
header is already exposed to browsers, so a future version can start
sending it without a CORS change that would silently hide it.

Sunset.description: Reserved, alongside `Deprecation`. Not sent by v1.

x-webhook-events.description:
We POST to your endpoint when something happens. The body is an event
object; the headers tell you which event it is and prove it came from us.

signature.algorithm:
`hash_hmac('sha256', timestamp . '.' . rawRequestBody, secret)`. Compute
it over the raw body, before any JSON parsing — re-encoding changes the
bytes and the signature will not match. Compare with a constant-time
comparison, and reject timestamps that are too old to stop replays.

headers.X-SendKuy-Event: The event name, the same value as `events` on the endpoint.
headers.X-SendKuy-Event-Id:
The id of this delivery attempt's event. It stays the same across all six
attempts, so use it to make your handler idempotent — a retry is the same
event, not a second one.

retries.description:
The first call is immediate; the five entries above are the waits before
each following attempt. Answer 2xx quickly — the call times out after 10
seconds, and a slow handler is a failed delivery. Repeated failures
eventually disable the endpoint, which shows up as `disabled_at`.

x-webhook-events.delivery_note:
`message.delivered` on a single message means the provider accepted it —
for WhatsApp, WhatsApp took it. It is raised once, at hand-off. When the
phone receives the message we fill `delivered_at`, and `read_at` once it
is read; read them with `GET /messages/{id}`, because no event is raised
when they arrive. Campaign messages also move to `delivered` and `opened`
as those receipts come in, and raise those events.
x-webhook-events.campaign_only_note:
The five marked `campaign_only` are only ever raised for messages born
from a campaign. The tables behind single sends do not record those
states at all, so subscribing to them and sending one-off messages means
waiting for events that will never arrive.
